Title: Is this the year Texas Democrats break their long losing streak in statewide elections?
Text:
A new survey shows James Talarico leading Ken Paxton for a U.S. Senate seat in Texas. And longtime Gov. Greg Abbott is in a neck-and-neck battle with his Democratic challenger to keep his job.

A University of Texas/Texas Politics Project poll, conducted Sept. 25 to Oct. 5 and published this week, framed the upcoming midterm as shaping up to be a “historically close election” in the Lone Star State.

Talarico, a state representative, leads Paxton, the state’s attorney general, 50% to 47%, which is within the poll’s margin of error.

Independents favor Talarico over Paxton by a wide margin, 69% to 11%.

And Talarico leads among Latino, urban, suburban and female voters.

Paxton leads among rural and male voters.

No Democrat has won a statewide election in Texas since 1994, but Talarico has a real shot at breaking that streak.

“It certainly is shaping up to be a perfect storm, a positive one if you're a Democrat, a negative one if you're a Republican,” said Mark Jones, a political scientist at Rice University in Houston.

Jones said that President Donald Trump’s unpopularity is the biggest contributing factor to a potential Democratic upset in Texas. He said Trump is close to 10 points underwater in Texas and about 20 points underwater nationally.

And he said that’s dragging down all Republican candidates this midterm election.

Jones said another important factor in the “perfect storm” is that the Republican Senate candidate, Paxton, is “deeply flawed.”

Paxton has faced years of legal and ethical controversies, including a resolved securities-fraud case and a 2023 impeachment – in which he was ultimately acquitted – over multiple accusations, including that he abused his office for private gain.

“It's tough to overestimate how truly bad a candidate Ken Paxton is on so many different levels,” Jones said. “That is, all of the political, financial, legal, marital, ethical baggage that he has really weighs him down. And just on the campaign trail, he just isn't very good.”

The UT/Texas Politics Project poll found likely Republican voters hold less favorable views of Paxton than likely Democratic voters do of their guy.

Sixty-nine percent of likely Republican voters view Paxton favorably. Meanwhile, 92% of likely Democratic voters view Talarico favorably.

Jones said that disparity is a killer for the GOP’s hopes of victory in the race.

And he said the lackluster support for Paxton among Republicans is probably more impactful to the race than Talarico's support among the limited number of swing voters.

Talarico told Sinclair politics reporter Mikenzie Frost that he’s “not interested in turning Texas blue.”

But he does want to flip the Senate seat.

“I want to win this seat so that I can fight for all 31 million Texans, whether they're Democrats, independents or Republicans,” Talarico said. “My party talks about turning Texas blue a lot. Republicans talk about keeping Texas red. I've said before, I think the best color for Texas is purple.”

And Jones said Talarico has enough money at his disposal to wage a formidable campaign against his Republican opponent.

The latest Federal Election Commission filings show Talarico’s campaign reported $68.6 million in total receipts from Sept. 8, 2025, through June 30, 2026, while Paxton’s reported about $9.25 million from April 1, 2025, through Sept. 30, 2026.

That’s the final part of the “perfect storm” that Jones said has made Talarico the “even-money favorite” to win.

The UT/Texas Politics Project poll found a large enthusiasm gap between Democratic and Republican voters, which Jones said could matter a lot.

The poll found 72% of Democrats are either “extremely” or “very” enthusiastic about voting this year, a 10-point advantage over Republicans.

But the poll also found the Democratic brand has its work cut out for it in Texas, with just 34% favorability compared to 41% for Republicans.

And Jones said Talarico is no shoo-in.

Jones said a defeat this time around would sting even harder for Democrats, given the optimism for the upset on the Democratic side.

“If Paxton wins, then that will be one of the most demoralizing defeats that Texas Democrats have suffered or experienced in a long string of demoralizing defeats,” Jones said.

OTHER TEXAS RACES, INCLUDING FOR GOVERNOR

The UT/Texas Politics Project poll showed Democratic state representative Gina Hinojosa leading Abbott by a point in the governor’s race.

If Abbott is reelected, it will be for a record fourth term.

Jones said Abbott is still likely to win, even if Hinojosa is giving him a strong challenge.

Texas Democratic gubernatorial candidate Gina Hinojosa speaks during a campaign event at Wooldridge Square on October 15, 2026, in Austin, Texas. (Photo by Jan Sonnenmair/Getty Images)

Jones said Abbott will saturate the airwaves in Texas with campaign ads between now and the election, and he said “there's a lot of ammunition” Abbott can use against Hinojosa politically, given her liberal voting record in the Texas House.

Jones said the most likely scenario is that Abbott still wins, albeit by a much smaller margin than in 2022.

Abbott won in 2022 with close to 55% of the vote, similar to the nearly 56% he won with in 2018.

FILE - Texas Gov. Greg Abbott speaks on stage on the second day of the 2026 Republican National Convention at the American Airlines Center on September 10, 2026, in Dallas. (Photo by Kevin Dietsch/Getty Images)

Among likely Republican voters, 89%, view Abbott favorably. A similar share of likely Democratic voters, 84%, view Hinojosa favorably.

While Jones thinks Talarico has a real shot at turning the Senate seat blue, he doesn’t see a blue wave coming to Texas this election.

Other than perhaps the railroad commissioner race, Jones said the rest of the statewide races are likely to stay in Republican hands.

Jones said that Republican railroad commissioner candidate Bo French made his election harder than it had to be when he made what were viewed as racist statements regarding UT students of South Asian origin.

That incident raised French’s profile, but in a negative way, Jones said.

And he said that French failed to go with “the smart strategy of just riding the Republican label to victory, which he could have done.”

The UT/Texas Politics Project poll noted that likely voters have little familiarity with most of the state’s down-ballot candidates, which Jones said favors Republicans.

But Jones said Republicans understand the risk they face if their voters aren’t motivated to head to the polls this election, given the enthusiasm gap found in this and other polls.

“You always are doing two things in the campaign. You're trying to mobilize your base, and you're trying to convince undecided voters or persuadable voters to vote your way. But right now, Republicans are starting to focus more of their energies on getting their people to turn out to vote,” Jones said. “That's why you see JD Vance in Tyler, Texas.”

Title: 'Deeply disturbing', India's envoy to US on mass shooting attempt at Hindu temple
Text:
WASHINGTON, Oct 15: India's ambassador to the US Vinay Mohan Kwatra on Thursday termed the attempted mass shooting at a Hindu temple near Chicago as "deeply disturbing" and said racist violence has no place in a civilised society.

Kwatra's remarks came a day after a teenager was arrested for allegedly plotting to carry out a "mass shooting" at a Hindu temple in the US state of Illinois.

"The attempted mass shooting at the Hindu temple in Aurora is deeply disturbing. Racist violence including anti-Hindu and anti-India hate has no place in a civilized society," Kwatra said in a post on X.

Advertisement

The US Assistant Attorney General Harmeet Dhillon said the Civil Rights Division of the Department of Justice will investigate the incident.

"Concerning. @CivilRights will review/investigate," Dhillon said in a post on X.

Several Indian diaspora groups have condemned the attempted mass shooting at a Hindu temple in Aurora, Illinois.

"This incident is a stark reminder that anti-India and anti-Hindu hatred is not merely online and political rhetoric -- it can translate into real world threats against our community and places of worship," Foundation for India and Indian Diaspora Studies (FIIDS) said.

Coalition of Hindus of North America (CoHNA) appealed to authorities to protect temples.

"We urge elected officials and law enforcement agencies to take the growing threats against Hindu places of worship seriously, strengthen protections, and unequivocally condemn Hinduphobia," the organisation said.

"We also call on temples and community organisations to review their security measures, remain vigilant, and promptly report suspicious activity," it added.

"There's also no question that the hate has gone from inchoate to a very coherent anti-Hindu animus that is now radicalising white supremacists online. The risk of online hate spilling into real world violence has never been higher," said Suhag Shukla, Executive Director, Hindu American Foundation.

Earlier this month, the Swaminarayan Hindu Temple Vadthaldham in greater Cleveland, Ohio, was vandalised by unidentified persons.

In 2025, a Hindu temple in Spanish Fork, Utah faced gunfire. Four temples in California and three in New York have been vandalised with hate slogans.

The Hanuman statue in Sugarland, Texas, has been facing regular calls to knock it down, CoHNA said. (PTI)

Title: Illinois incident adds to growing concerns over racist hostility, anti-India hate in US: MEA
Text:
NEW DELHI, Oct 15 : India on Thursday said it was deeply concerned by reports of an alleged plot to carry out a mass shooting targeting a Hindu temple in Illinois in the US and underlined that the incident adds to growing concerns over "racist hostility and anti-India hate" in that country.

Ministry of External Affairs Spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal said this in a statement in response to media queries related to the attempted mass shooting incident near Chicago.

A teenager was arrested on October 11 and charged with making a terrorist threat and unlawful possession of a weapon.

Advertisement

According to investigators, the youth had tried to open fire "potentially targeting" the place of worship in the Aurora city in Illinois, but his gun jammed, forcing him to drive back home, a move that prevented a mass murder.

"We are deeply concerned by reports of an alleged plot to carry out a mass shooting targeting a Hindu temple in the Aurora area of Illinois. The reported anti-Hindu and racist nature of the alleged plot, including references to violence against people of Indian origin, is particularly disturbing," Jaiswal said in his statement.

He said the MEA has taken note of the action taken by US law enforcement authorities, including the arrest and detention of the suspect and the charges brought against him.

"This incident adds to growing concerns over racist hostility and anti-India hate in the US. There is a need for greater vigilance, zero tolerance for hate-motivated violence, and decisive action to ensure the safety and security of the Indian community," he said.

"We expect US authorities to thoroughly investigate the matter, bring those responsible to justice and take all necessary measures to prevent such incidents," the MEA spokesperson said.

Alexandros Paporakis, 19, of Palatine village was arrested, with investigators recovering a manifesto expressing white supremacist ideology and references to violence against people of Indian descent.

India's Ambassador to the US, Vinay Mohan Kwatra, on Thursday termed the attempted mass shooting at the Hindu temple as "deeply disturbing" and said racist violence has no place in a civilised society. (PTI)
